info.name: PROG2002 A2 - Charity Events API
info.description:
Read-only REST API for the charity events website.

Built for PROG2002 Web Development II, Assessment 2.

Data source : MySQL 8.4, database charityevents_db
Base URL    : http://localhost:3000/api

The API is read-only in Assessment 2: the brief states that POST, PUT and DELETE
methods belong to Assessment 3, so no write requests are included here.

Suggested demo order for the video:
  1. Health check
  2. Home page listing (upcoming events)
  3. Search with all three criteria at once
  4. The deliberately invalid date range, to show the 400 response
  5. The suspended event, to show that it is hidden (404)

item.name: Validation and error handling
item.description: Requests that are expected to fail. Run these in the video to show that the API validates its input and never exposes a suspended event.

item.name: /events  (invalid date range)  -> 400
item.description: EXPECTED TO FAIL with 400. The response names the field that was wrong, which is what lets the search page show a message beside the form.

query.description: Earlier than from, which is refused.

request.description: EXPECTED TO FAIL with 400. The response names the field that was wrong, which is what lets the search page show a message beside the form.

item.name: /events  (impossible date)  -> 400
item.description: EXPECTED TO FAIL with 400. Shows that a date is checked as a real calendar date, not merely as text in the right shape.

request.description: EXPECTED TO FAIL with 400. Shows that a date is checked as a real calendar date, not merely as text in the right shape.

item.name: /events  (unknown sort key)  -> 400
item.description: EXPECTED TO FAIL with 400. The sort parameter is chosen from a fixed list rather than interpolated into the SQL, so an injection attempt is rejected before any query runs.

query.description: An attempt to inject SQL through the sort parameter.

request.description: EXPECTED TO FAIL with 400. The sort parameter is chosen from a fixed list rather than interpolated into the SQL, so an injection attempt is rejected before any query runs.

item.name: /events/11  (suspended event)  -> 404
item.description: EXPECTED TO FAIL with 404. Event 11 exists in the events table but its status is suspended, so the public API behaves as though it does not exist. This is the clearest single piece of evidence that the visibility rule is enforced in the database view rather than in the page.

request.description: EXPECTED TO FAIL with 404. Event 11 exists in the events table but its status is suspended, so the public API behaves as though it does not exist. This is the clearest single piece of evidence that the visibility rule is enforced in the database view rather than in the page.

exec: pm.test('the suspended event is not disclosed', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().success).to.be.false);
